DL5SBM-9356 and when he reached in front of Tikona Park, Loni Road, Shahdara, Delhi, driver of a Santro Car bearing registration no. DL2CAD-5968 (in short "offending vehicle") while driving it at a high speed, rashly and negligently in the process of overtaking the motorcycle, hit the motorcycle on Dar - Vinay Aggarwal vs Jishan on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141775323/
1 its right side, due to which petitioner fell down from the motorcycle and sustained injuries.

sentences.text: The offending car was got stopped by the public persons.
Police came and in PCR van, injured was removed to GTB Hospital, Delhi, where his MLC was prepared.
In connection with the accident, FIR no.133/2018, under sections 279/337 IPC was registered at PS Shahdara.

During the investigation,
it was revealed that at the time of accident, offending vehicle was not insured and it was being driven by respondent no.1 Jishan (CCL, aged 17 years) and owned by respondent no.2 Shakir Saifi.

After completion of investigation, respondent no.1 (CCL) was charge-sheeted under sections 279/338 IPC and 3/181 of Motor Vehicle Act, whereas, separate Kalandara under sections 5/180 and 146/192 of Motor Vehicle Act was made against father of CCL.
3 . A t t h e t i m e o f f i l i n g o f D A R , b o t h t h e r e s p o n d e n t s a p p e a r e d i n ______________________________________________________________________ person

In absence of written- statement of respondents, issues could not be framed and matter was adjourned for evidence of the petitioner.

iii). PW3 Dr. Nadeem, CMO, GTB Hospital, Delhi deposed that he had examined the injured vide MLC (already exhibited as Ex.PW1/F).
iv).

PW4 Dr. Rahul Kumar, Senior Resident, Department of Orthopedics, GTB Hospital, Delhi produced the record pertaining to disability certificate no.
80/80/01/2020, dated 29.01.2020 of the petitioner and proved it as Ex.PW4/A to Dar - Vinay Aggarwal vs Jishan on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141775323/

5.
It is seen that the petitioner got himself examined as PW1 and testified by way of his affidavit Ex.PW1/1 on the lines of the FIR which he had got lodged on the basis of his statement made to police.

PW1/ injured categorically deposed that the accident took place due to reckless and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the respondent no.1, who was arrested by the police of PS Shahdara and offending vehicle was seized from the spot.

The testimony of PW1/ injured has remained unchallenged as this witness was not cross- examined on behalf of the respondents, who neither filed reply/ written-statement nor led any evidence in their defence.
Since the testimony of the petitioner has remained uncontroverted, the same has to be accepted on its face value itself.

6. Further, on perusal of the DAR, this Tribunal finds that the FIR was registered within two hours o f t h e a c c i d e n t , w h e r e i n r e g i s t r a t i o n ______________________________________________________________________ number of the offending vehicle is clearly mentioned.

Further, it is observed that the vehicles involved in the accident i.e. the offending vehicle as well as the motorcycle of the injured, which were found at the spot in accidental condition as per FIR, were seized from the spot of accident itself vide respective seizure memos, which have been placed on record being part of the DAR.

And mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle and that of the motorcycle of the injured,
which also form part of the DAR, clearly show the accidental damages, which further supports the case of the petitioner.
The driver Jishan (CCL) in the offending vehicle was caught hold by the public persons and handed over to the police at the place of accident itself.

The Apprehension Memo,
prepared by the Investigating Officer in this regard, proves the said fact.
7. Further, there is no challenge from the respondent no.1/ driver of the offending vehicle to the version of the petitioner.

The respondent no.1 was the best witness, who could have stepped into the witness box to challenge the testimony of the injured (PW1) regarding the above accident and its manner but neither he filed a reply to the claim petition nor preferred to enter into the witness box during the course of inquiry.

Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by him in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. v. Kamlesh, 2009(3) AD (Delhi) 310.
8 . sentences.text: Moreover, it is settled proposition of law that in an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine-qua-non.

However,
the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of the preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

However, that does not mean that a Tribunal which has been approached with a claim for compensation under the Motor Vehicle Act should ignore all basic principles of law in determining the claim for compensation.
The relevant provisions of the Act are not intended to jettison all principles of law relating to a claim for compensation which is still based on a tortious liability.

sentences.text: 11 . Thus, in view of the above, this Tribunal finds that there is sufficient material on record to establish that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1 and that resulted into grievous injuries to the petitioner.

COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 12. Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be a pittance.
"Just compensation" cannot be equated with bonanza but it suggests application of fair and equitable principles and reasonable approach of the Tribunal while awarding the compensation.
This reasonableness must be on a large peripheral field.

A man is not compensated for the physical injury which he might have received in the accident caused by the motor vehicle in a public place, rather he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury that he suffered in the accident.

[Ref. Yadava Kumar v. National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
( 2 0 1 0 ) 1 0 S C C 3 4 ; R a j K u m a r v . A j a y K u m a r ,
______________________________________________________________________ (2011) 1 SCC 343; Puttamma v. K.L. Narayana Reddy, (2013) 15 SCC 45].

sentences.text: 13. The present claim petition pertains to injury and scope of compensation in injury cases has been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/S Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755.

entities.text: R.D. Hattangadi v. M/S Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant extract is as under:
"Broadly speaking while fixing an amount of compensation payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and special damages.

Pecuniary damages are those which the victim has actually incurred and which is capable of being calculated in terms of money-, whereas non-pecuniary Dar - Vinay Aggarwal vs Jishan on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141775323/
4 damages are those which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

In order to appreciate two concepts pecuniary damages may, include expenses incurred by the claimant: (i) medical attendance; (ii) loss of earning of profit up to the date of trial; (iii) other material losses.

So far non-pecuniary damages are concerned, they may include (i) damages for mental and physical shock, pain and suffering, already suffered or likely to be suffered in future; (ii) damages to compensate for the loss of amenities of life which may include a variety of matters i.e.
on account of injury the claimant may not be able to walk, run or sit; (iii) damages for the loss of expectation of life, i.e. on account of injury the normal longevity of the person concerned is shortened; (iv) inconvenience, discomfort, disappointment,
hardship, frustration and mental stress in life."
14. Further, in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India laid down general principles for computation of compensation in injury cases.

entities.text: Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant p a r a s  
o f ______________________________________________________________________ the judgment are reproduced as under:
"4. The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.

5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:
Pecuniary Damages (Special Damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising:
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment.
Dar - Vinay Aggarwal vs Jishan on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141775323/
5
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.
Non-Pecuniary Damages (general damages)
(iv) Damages to pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.

( v ) L o s s o f a m e n i t i e s ( a n d / o r l o s s o f p r o s p e c t s o f m a r r i a g e )
_____________________________________________________________________ (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).

In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii)(a) and (iv).
It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)
(b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life."
15.

In the light of the aforementioned judgments, the compensation to which the petitioner is entitled shall be as under:-
PECUNIARY DAMAGES :
Medical Expenses 16.

Though the petitioner (PW1) has deposed in his affidavit of evidence that he had incurred more than Rs.1,00,000/- as medical expenses, however, he neither placed on record nor exhibited any medical bill in support of his claim.
Hence, the petitioner cannot be granted any compensation under this head.

Loss of earning during treatment:
17.
As per original discharge summary placed on record, the petitioner was diagnosed to have sustained "closed fracture of SOF (R)".

He remained hospitalized in GTB Hospital from 28.04.2018 to 08.05.2018 and thereafter also, his further treatment continued in OPD of GTB Hospital, where he lastly visited on 01.09.2018, as per medical documents placed on record.

The discharge summary s h o w s t h a t t h e p e t i t i o n e r w a s a d v i s e d b e d r e s t f o r o n e m o n t h . T h e O P D ____________________________________________________________________
__ prescription dated 02.06.2018 and 04.08.2018 also show that he was advised further rest.

Besides,
the bank statement filed along with the written arguments reflects that last salary (part salary) from petitioner's employer 'Pee Gee International' was credited into the bank account of the petitioner on Dar - Vinay Aggarwal vs Jishan on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141775323/
6 15.05.2018 and thereafter, no amount was credited to his account for about five months till 11.10.2018 when Rs.20,534/- was transferred to his account from 'Ezee Flight S Travel' (probably new employer).

Thus, keeping in view the nature of injury and the period of treatment, it may be safely assumed that injured would not have been in a position to resume his work for at least five months after the accident and therefore, he is entitled to be compensated for the said period.

18. The petitioner (PW1) has placed on record copy of his ITRs for the assessment year 2015-16,
2016-17 and 2017-18 and proved the same as Ex.PW1/D (colly).

Further, at the time of the final stage, learned counsel for the petitioner filed written arguments and along with the written arguments, he also placed on record copy of bank statement of the petitioner, copy of petitioner's ITR for the assessment year 2018-19 and copy of office Identity Card of the petitioner.

A perusal of the office Identity Card, issued by "Pee Gee International, 2381, Bihari Colony, Shahdara,
Delhi-110032" shows that the petitioner was working with the said employer as "Accountant".
Though
the best piece of the evidence of the income of petitioner was his pay slips for the months prior to the accident but the same have not been placed on record and instead ITRs have been filed.
I n t h e c i r c u m s t a n c e s , t h e I T R o f a s s e s s m e n t y e a r 2 0 1 8 - 1 9 w h i c h p e r t a i n s t o

______________________________________________________________________ the period from 01.04.2017 to 31.03.2018, is the most relevant piece of documents to assess the income of deceased because said ITR relates to the assessment year preceding the year in which accident happened on 28.04.2018, which shows the annual salary income of the petitioner from employer 'Pee Gee International' as Rs.3,08,003/- and accordingly, monthly income of the petitioner prior to the accident is assessed to be Rs.25,667/-.

Therefore, a sum of Rs.1,28,335/-
(25,667x5) is granted to the petitioner on account of loss of income of five months during treatment.

Loss of Future Earnings Due to Disability:
19.
The broad criteria for ascertaining the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity of the injured has been given in case of Raj Kumar (supra).

Further, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pappu Deo Yadav v. Naresh Kumar, (2022) 13 SCC 790, has cautioned the Claims Tribunal regarding mechanically applying the percentage of permanent disability as a percentage of economic loss or loss of earning capacity.

entities.text: Pappu Deo Yadav v. Naresh Kumar, (2022) 13 SCC 790
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the said judgment observed that in most of the cases, the percentage of economic loss, that is, the percentage of loss of earning capacity,
arising from a permanent disability will be different from the percentage of permanent disability.

20. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the said judgment further observed that what requires to be assessed by the Claims Tribunal is the effect of the permanent disability on the earning capacity of t h e i n j u r e d ; a n d a f t e r a s s e s s i n g t h e l o s s o f e a r n i n g c a p a c i t y i n t e r m s o f a ___________________________________________________________________
___ percentage of the income, it has to be quantified in terms of money, to arrive at the future loss of earnings (by applying the standard multiplier method used to determine loss of dependency).

However, in some cases, on appreciation of evidence and assessment, the Tribunal may find that the percentage of loss of earning capacity as a result of the permanent disability, is approximately the same as the percentage of permanent disability in which case, of course, the Tribunal will adopt the said percentage for determination of compensation.

That the crucial factor which has to be taken Dar - Vinay Aggarwal vs Jishan on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141775323/
7 into consideration, as per the Hon'ble Supreme Court, is to assess as to whether the permanent disability has any adverse effect on the earning capacity of the injured.

entities.text: Dar - Vinay Aggarwal vs Jishan on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A person who is engaged and cannot freely move to attend to his duties may not be able to match the earning in comparison with the one who is healthy and bodily abled.

21. In the instant case, PW4 Dr. Rahul Kumar has proved on record the disability certificate issued to the petitioner as Ex.PW4/A, as per which, the petitioner has suffered 9% permanent disability in relation to the right lower limb.

In response to the Court Question that as to what difficulty the petitioner will face in his daily routine works due to this disability, the doctor (PW2) replied that he had not assessed the patient, so he cannot comment upon the same.

Admittedly, prior to the accident, the petitioner was working as Accountant with 'Pee Gee International', Shahdara, Delhi and as discussed above under the head of "loss of earnings during treatment", the petitioner after about five months of his accident had resumed earnings from another employer as is clearly r e f l e c t e d f r o m t h e b a n k a c c o u n t s t a t e m e n t ______________________________________________________________________ which shows the entries qua credit of amount in his bank account from 'Ezee Flight S Travel'
(probably the new employer) on a regular basis every month from the month of October-2018 onward and therefore, it cannot be said the petitioner has been suffering loss of income due to aforesaid permanent disability which he sustained as a result of the accident.
22. In view of the above, the functional disability of the petitioner is considered as nil.
As such, the petitioner is not entitled to any compensation under this head.

Special Diet & Conveyance Charge:
23.

The discharge summary which has been placed on record in original shows that during hospitalization from 28.04.2018 to 08.05.2018 in GTB Hospital, the petitioner had to undergo surgery (ORIF with IMILN 40x 10 mm).

After being discharged from the hospital, he remained under OPD treatment and had to make a number of visits to the hospital till September-2018 for his further treatment, as per medical documents placed on record.

Thus, considering the nature of injury and period of treatment, it can be safely inferred that the petitioner had to spend a reasonable amount on high and rich protein diet for the purpose of early recovery apart from incurring transport charges for visiting the hospital's OPD on a number of occasions for his further treatment and therefore, a notional sum of Rs.25,000/- is awarded under this head.

Attendant Charge:
2 4 . T h o u g h n o d o c u m e n t a r y e v i d e n c e h a s b e e n l e d r e g a r d i n g h i r i n g ______________________________________________________________________ professional attendants during treatment but it cannot be ignored that keeping in view the nature of injury suffered by the petitioner, his family members would have to render their services for providing assistance to the petitioner in his routine activities and due to that their work/ job would definitely have suffered.

For claiming compensation, necessity of employing a professional attendant/ care taker is not required and the petitioner should be compensated for the value of the Dar - Vinay Aggarwal vs Jishan on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141775323/
8 services of the family members, which has been or would be necessitated by the wrong doing of the driver. (Refer : DTC & Ors Vs. Lalita, 1983 ACJ 253).

sentences.text: Accordingly, the petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.25,000/- under this head.

NON PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
Pain & Sufferings:
25.

While discussing the criteria to ascertain the compensation for pain and sufferings by victims of vehicular accident, observations of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Satya Narain v. Jai Kishan, FAO No:
709/02, date of decision: 02.02.2007 can be considered:
"12. On account of pain and suffering, suffice would it be to note that it is difficult to measure pain and suffering in terms of a money value.
However, compensation which has to be paid must bear some objective co-relation with the pain and suffering.

13. The objective facts relatable to pain and suffering would be:
(a) Nature of injury.
(b) Body part affected (c) Duration of the treatment."
2 6 . I n t h e i n s t a n t c a s e , t h e M L C o f i n j u r e d , p r e p a r e d a t G T B H o s p i t a l ,
______________________________________________________________________ Delhi shows that he suffered grievous injuries.

As per discharge summary, he was diagnosed to have sustained closed fracture of SOF (R) i.e. fracture in his right leg for treatment of which, he had to remain hospitalized from 28.04.2018 to 08.05.2018 and had to undergo surgery.
Even after being discharged from the hospital, he had to make a number of visits to the doctor for his further treatment.

Thus, it is clear that due to the injuries sustained in the accident, the petitioner/ injured must have gone through immense pain and suffering during his treatment and therefore, a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded to the petitioner under this head.

INTEREST 28.
The petitioner shall also be entitled for the interest @ 6% per annum on the award amount from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of realization.
LIABILITY 29.

Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents is liable to pay the compensation a m o u n t . A d m i t t e d l y , t h e o f f e n d i n g v e h i c l e ______________________________________________________________________ was not insured at the time of accident and therefore, the respondent no.1, being the driver of the offending vehicle is the principal tortfeasor whereas, respondent no.2, being registered owner would have the vicarious liability.

Had the respondent no.1, been a major on the date of the accident the respondent no.1 and 2 would have been liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner and their liability would have remain joint and several.

But as the respondent no.1 was a minor on the date of the accident, he could have been represented only through his father/ guardian and he could have been fastened with liability only if so represented through his father/ guardian.

30. The record reveals that though the minor driver has been shown as respondent no.1, however, it was his father who was present before the Tribunal on 18.07.2018 i.e., the 1st date of hearing before this Tribunal.
On 25.09.2018 also it was the father of the respondent no.1 who was present before the Tribunal and after the said date none on behalf of the respondent appeared on any dates of the hearing.
31. In the opinion of this Tribunal, in the case where one of the respondents was a minor, he ought to have been represented through his guardian ad litem.

In the present case, there has been substantial compliance of the same as the minor respondent no.1 never appeared before this Tribunal on any dates of hearing and whatever appearances were made on his behalf, were made through his father.

The respondent no.1, being minor, was duly represented by his father/ natural g u a r d i a n a n d a c c o r d i n g l y , n o p r e j u d i c e o f a n y k i n d ______________________________________________________________________ was caused to the minor.
Accordingly, the respondent no.1 and respondent no.2 shall be jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award.
RELIEF 32.
In the light of the above discussion, the present claim petition is allowed and the following award is passed:

AWARD Dar - Vinay Aggarwal vs Jishan on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141775323/

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The respondent no.1 was the best witness, who could have stepped into the witness box to challenge the testimony of the injured (PW1) regarding the above accident and its manner but neither he filed a reply to the claim petition nor preferred to enter into the witness box during the course of inquiry.
Moreover, it is settled proposition of law that in an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine-qua-non.
However,
the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of the preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
However, that does not mean that a Tribunal which has been approached with a claim for compensation under the Motor Vehicle Act should ignore all basic principles of law in determining the claim for compensation.
SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303, Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Meena Variyal & Ors., (2007) 5 SCC 428.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be a pittance.
"Just compensation" cannot be equated with bonanza but it suggests application of fair and equitable principles and reasonable approach of the Tribunal while awarding the compensation.
13. The present claim petition pertains to injury and scope of compensation in injury cases has been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/S Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755.

He remained hospitalized in GTB Hospital from 28.04.2018 to 08.05.2018 and thereafter also, his further treatment continued in OPD of GTB Hospital, where he lastly visited on 01.09.2018, as per medical documents placed on record.
Thus, keeping in view the nature of injury and the period of treatment, it may be safely assumed that injured would not have been in a position to resume his work for at least five months after the accident and therefore, he is entitled to be compensated for the said period.
Further, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pappu Deo Yadav v. Naresh Kumar, (2022) 13 SCC 790, has cautioned the Claims Tribunal regarding mechanically applying the percentage of permanent disability as a percentage of economic loss or loss of earning capacity.
A person who is engaged and cannot freely move to attend to his duties may not be able to match the earning in comparison with the one who is healthy and bodily abled.
As such, the petitioner is not entitled to any compensation under this head.
After being discharged from the hospital, he remained under OPD treatment and had to make a number of visits to the hospital till September-2018 for his further treatment, as per medical documents placed on record.
Thus, considering the nature of injury and period of treatment, it can be safely inferred that the petitioner had to spend a reasonable amount on high and rich protein diet for the purpose of early recovery apart from incurring transport charges for visiting the hospital's OPD on a number of occasions for his further treatment and therefore, a notional sum of Rs.25,000/- is awarded under this head.
